clue.text: Not to be swallowed (even with colder extremities removed)

parts.note: surface reading: food that cannot be eaten
setter's reading: the word for a tall story that cannot be believed still means uneatable once the outer letters of colder, C and R, are taken out

explanation.surface: A warning about something inedible, even once the chilliest bits have been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: INCREDIBLE means a story you cannot swallow; remove C and R, the ends of colder, and INEDIBLE is left, food you cannot swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is idiomatically to believe it, so something unbelievable is a claim nobody could accept.

clue.text: Railwaymen prepared, one hears, to hold points for tender

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so the compass letters sit within

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen

indicators.note: says the word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: prepared means made
two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Train workers got ready to hold a station's points for the tender car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like a railway coal wagon, matching the surface, but it is a noun for one who tends.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid looks after young children, so she is a carer, one who tends others.

clue.text: Head off schism to some extent

indicators.note: cutting the head off removes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a breach is a split or rift

explanation.surface: Heading off a split in the group, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' reads as a hedging phrase, but 'some extent' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reach is the range or scope of something, how far its influence spreads.

clue.text: Diverts drivers in races through Norfolk town

indicators.note: in places the motoring club inside the races
running through the town means sitting inside its name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Motorists are sent off course as a race passes through a country town.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract someone is to draw their attention away elsewhere, turning it aside.

clue.text: Mounting transport disorder one cause for complaint

definitions.note: singular here, the answer is plural

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
an ill is an ailment or disorder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Rising transport chaos is the main grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble, but it is an illness, which germs cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, many of them disease-causing germs, so they bring on a medical complaint.

clue.text: Offence often linked to trial

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wrong or transgression
second meaning: the partner word in the phrase about learning by experiment

explanation.surface: A crime that tends to end up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' suggests a court case, but the phrase is 'trial and error'.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake or wrong act, and it follows 'trial and' in the familiar idiom.

clue.text: Author securing second advance

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the writer's name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A writer obtains a second payment ahead of publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' reads as money paid to an author, but it is a verb: to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose a question or theory is to put it forward for consideration, which is advancing it.

clue.text: Unfinished spat with Europe, possibly, the cause of bad atmosphere

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the quarrel word loses its final letter
possibly means in one of several possible forms, so the letters can be rearranged

parts.note: spat, a quarrel, without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unresolved quarrel with Europe is souring relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad atmosphere' reads as diplomatic tension, but it is literal air: a thick London fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense yellowish fog, like the old London smogs, which makes the air foul.

clue.text: Track succeeded without much financial support

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
having little money

explanation.surface: A railway line went ahead without much funding.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of footprints or droppings left by an animal, which hunters follow.

clue.text: Terrible crisis at extremely old age

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful emergency strikes someone in their extreme old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely old age' sounds like a person's dotage, but it is a geological period.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triassic is a geological period around two hundred million years back, an era of truly ancient times.

clue.text: Ground leader of treachery abandoned

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word that follows, the one singled out to go
what is abandoned is left behind, so that front letter drops out of the word

parts.note: treason is betrayal of one's country

explanation.surface: A battlefield where the commander of a betrayal has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like land or terrain, but it is grounds in the sense of a basis for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground for doing something is a justification or motive behind it, and so is a reason.

clue.text: At the end of it one's bound to be exhausted

definitions.text: At the end of it one's bound to be exhausted

parts.words: At the end of it one's bound
parts.note: setter's reading: an animal tied on a rope is bound at the far end of it
surface reading: the idiom about being at the end of your patience or strength

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'at the end of one's tether' means having no patience or strength left; literally, a tethered animal is tied at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or chain used to tie an animal so it cannot roam is what the bound creature hangs from.

clue.text: Old port run by US City Council

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a board is a governing council

explanation.surface: A historic harbour managed by an American city's council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests a harbour town, but it is the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the former sailing term for the left-hand side of a vessel, later replaced by port.

clue.text: Artist's beginning in style of primitive art

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: dub is a style of reggae-based music

indicators.note: a beginning is where a word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word artist

explanation.surface: How a painter got started in the crude manner of early cave pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A daub is a crude, unskilled painting, the sort of rough work called primitive.

clue.text: A feature topped by unadorned canopy

indicators.note: in a down clue, being topped by means the other piece goes above, written first

parts.note: bald means plain, bare
taken as written
a facial feature

explanation.surface: An architectural feature crowned by a plain overhead cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' reads as part of a building, but it is a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldachin is an ornamental canopy over an altar, throne or doorway, often of fabric or stone.

clue.text: Presenting no acting difficulty in Peter Pan, say

definitions.note: a phrase meaning 'easy'; the answer is a noun for an easy task
definitions.meaning: first meaning: something very easy to do
second meaning: a stage play written for children, as J M Barrie's is

explanation.surface: Playing a part in Peter Pan is no challenge for an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' sits inside the first meaning to tie it to the theatre; the second meaning reads the answer literally as a play for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that needs no effort is called child's play, and Peter Pan is a drama written for young audiences.

clue.text: Girl, taking earnest of engagement, though uncertain

definitions.note: an adjective here; the answer is a participle used the same way

indicators.note: the girl takes the token, which joins on after her name

parts.note: Di, short for Diana
the ring is the pledge, or earnest, given at an engagement

explanation.surface: A girl accepts an engagement token though she is still having doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: An earnest is a pledge given as a sign of a bargain to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering means hesitating or wavering, unable to make a decision, so being undecided.

clue.text: For No. Ten a new PM

indicators.note: new means made over in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the full stop

explanation.surface: Downing Street gets a new Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like Prime Minister, matching No. Ten (Downing Street), but it is post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: PM is post meridiem, the abbreviation used for times after midday.

clue.text: Teenager getting financial help in rise

indicators.note: in puts the benefit payment inside the word for climbing

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A young person receives an increase in their allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person between childhood and adulthood, the age group of thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Left out of education, deservedly so

definitions.note: the answer is getting something one deserves

indicators.note: out of says the letter is taken away from the following word

parts.note: learning is education
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone justly left out of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deservedly so' stands for gaining something one has merited, which is earning.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning means gaining something through work or merit, so receiving it as is deserved.

clue.text: Utterly correct ceremonial

definitions.note: a noun here: a ceremonial is a formal ritual

indicators.note: read as 'in an uttered way', meaning spoken out rather than spelt

parts.note: correct means right

explanation.surface: A formal ceremony done in a thoroughly proper way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like an intensifier meaning completely, but it signals the word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a solemn religious or ceremonial act, and a ceremonial is the formal procedure for one.

clue.text: One selling or telling stories, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shopkeeper who sells goods to the public
second meaning: to retail a story is to recount it, so a teller of tales

explanation.surface: A salesman who might also be spinning yarns.
explanation.walkthrough: To retail gossip or a story is to pass it on in detail; 'perhaps' flags that this sense of the word is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer sells goods to customers in shops, and to retail a story also means to recount it.

clue.text: Outcast from English side joining the French

indicators.note: joining means the French article attaches to the end of what goes before

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a cricket or football team of eleven, written as Roman numerals
le is French for the

explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone banished from their homeland, a person cast out.

clue.text: Sin — line taken on part of the Church

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
the apse is the rounded recess at a church's east end

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing committed in one section of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a moral slip or failing, a minor wrongdoing like a sin.

clue.text: Opposing players take heart to give repeat performance

indicators.note: the players take on the following piece, which joins after them

parts.note: East and North are opponents at the bridge table
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Rival performers summon their courage to play the piece again.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South partner East and West, so E and N sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is an extra item performed at the audience's demand, typically a repeat of something already played.

clue.text: Church member joining appeal

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
a member is a limb

explanation.surface: A churchgoer takes part in a fund-raising drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a congregation member, but it is a limb; 'appeal' is attractiveness, not a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is attractiveness or allure, the quality of being pleasing to others.

clue.text: Piece work taken on by mistake

explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece work' reads as paid-by-the-item labour, but 'Piece' alone is the definition, a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop is one of the chessmen, moving diagonally across the board, so it is a playing piece.

clue.text: Impressionist art I omit to review

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist is an entertainer who mimics famous people's voices and mannerisms, which is a copier.

clue.text: American worker of old in corral

clue.text: A promise of action

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pledge, especially to marry
second meaning: a military battle or fight

explanation.surface: A pledge that something will be done.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is both a formal pledge, as to marry, and a battle between armed forces.
